statement: For every negative full once-punctured-torus outer involution, killing its actual cusp reflection gives exactly the coinvariants of the full rank-two homology module. This quotient is Zhat x C2 in the identity-modulo-two case and Zhat otherwise. Killing all finite-order elements gives exactly Zhat in both cases, with an explicit quotient map taking every chosen cusp transporter to 1 or 2 respectively. The quotient has a continuous section inside F; in the two-section case it has a section inside the fixed group of the other section, giving an actual embedded Zhat x C2 subgroup.
depends_on: D43 global negative involution multiplier; D58 actual cusp fusion, full section classes and distinguishing Bockstein character; D59 full fixed homology line and the other section's fixed-group surjection
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Both quotient morphisms are constructed explicitly, and the finite factor is detected by the actual D58 section character normalized to vanish on the chosen cusp reflection.
notes: The identity c=[g,v] implies that killing v kills the commutator c. The quotient therefore factors through F abelianization, and the reverse map f v^epsilon -> [f] modulo (A-I) proves the exact isomorphism. In the homology basis ([g],e), A has matrix [[1,a],[0,-1]]. If a is divisible by two, the coinvariant map is (r,t)->(r+(a/2)t,t mod2); otherwise it is (r,t)->2r+at. Their kernels are exactly Zhat(a,-2). The D58 character b+b(v)u sends the other section to the unique nonzero C2 element, so the normal closure of all torsion is exactly the kernel of the displayed Zhat quotient. A preimage of 1 in F gives a continuous profinite-power splitting; D59 allows this preimage inside the other fixed group in the two-class case. No full free-product presentation, full fixed-group recognition or geometric conjugacy is inferred.
computational_checks: work/part_c/code/torus_torsion_quotient_d60.py and its adjacent JSON/stdout certificate: exhaustive finite coefficient-ring checks of the involution matrices, the exact kernel/image equalities, the quotient sizes and transporter-coordinate values.
